disposition_reason: The registered task re-estimates feeding effects on ripple power, duration and NREM-normalized rates. The paper reports biological contrasts, correlations and mediation, not a predictive method with an ordered performance score. Larger feeding effects or smaller p-values would alter the scientific finding rather than surpass the paper. The preserved runtime explicitly measures archived-report fidelity, which is calibration only.

source_paper.title: Food intake enhances hippocampal sharp wave-ripples

evidence.locator: Results; Figures 1–3; Methods: Data processing, analyses, and sleep scoring; Animals; Food restriction and experimental procedures
evidence.supports: The source studies pre/post-meal physiological changes, defines detection and session-level ratios, and identifies different experimental cohorts. It supplies no prediction or reconstruction accuracy benchmark.

Author deposit lists all-done.mat, 2022food_safe.xlsx, MainAnalysisScript.m, extractRippleAndFPStructs4.m, detectRipples.m and SleepQuantificationFeb2025.m. Inventory inspection does not establish raw-input completeness or archive-to-figure mapping.

target.description: Estimate pre/post-feeding changes in hippocampal SWR power, duration and rate, and their association with meal amount and sleep depth. This is an observational/experimental biological effect-estimation task.

dataset.description: Author release Data and code for Kaya et al. (2025), Figshare article 28691093 version 1. The historical task uses processed event/session structs in all-done.mat; raw-to-event inference is outside that preserved scope.

cohort.description: The paper distinguishes food-restricted chow, ad-libitum chocolate and Jello cohorts; Figure 2 reports nine animals/39 sessions and Figure 3 reports 7/9/10 animals across its conditions. The registration records 95 released sessions/10 animals, but their exact mapping to each paper figure and condition code was not verified from primary metadata.

split.description: The source compares paired pre/post sleep sessions and experimental food conditions; it defines no train/validation/test split or held-out prediction contest. A new animal split would introduce a new evaluation task.

inputs.description: For the preserved processed-event scope: author event/session ripple measurements, food conditions, NREM durations and animal/session identifiers. The deposit also lists analysis helpers; it does not by itself establish access to complete raw LFP and sleep-scoring inputs.

preprocessing.description: Source detection uses NREM only, excludes sessions with under 30 minutes sleep, filters LFP at 150–250 Hz, and requires peaks at least 5 SD with at least 40 ms above 1 SD. Pre/post comparisons use session means and postsleep/presleep ratios. Processed archive reproduction must preserve the originating detector and condition dictionary.

metric.description: Ripple fold changes, meal correlations and mediation coefficients describe physiology. None is an ordered method-performance loss whose improvement establishes a paper win.

aggregation.description: Paper analyses form session-level pre/post ratios; condition comparisons and captions distinguish animal and session counts. Repeated events and sessions cannot be silently promoted to independent animals.

comparison.primary_metric: No eligible ordered method-performance metric for the registered feeding-effect estimand

published_baseline.description: Reported correlations (including Figure 1 meal/power association) and p-values are biological findings, not baseline scores to beat.

reproduced_author_baseline.description: An exact replay of author effects or archived summaries is a calibration outcome and cannot supply a stronger-than-paper score.

minimum_effect.rationale: No meaningful superiority margin exists for increasing an observed biological effect estimate or its statistical significance.

uncertainty.method: No improvement test is admitted; historical analyses retain their inferential interpretation.
uncertainty.independent_unit: Animals, with repeated sessions and events nested within animals
uncertainty.rationale: Dependence-aware uncertainty can strengthen an audit, but changing uncertainty or attaining a smaller p-value is not an ordered same-task performance win.

paper_win_requires: This registration cannot admit an improvement win while its target remains reproduction or re-estimation of feeding-related physiological effects.

Any proposed predictive benchmark needs a separately reviewed source task, original performance comparator and registration; neither a new split nor archive-summary agreement may be relabelled as surpassing this paper.

current_sota.description: No current-SOTA comparison is defined for this descriptive task.

episode.improvement_loop: Inactive for paper-superiority scoring. Historical reanalysis may be retained as calibration and scientific critique.
episode.candidate_freeze: No active improvement episode is admitted for this source task.
episode.final_evaluation: Do not convert archived-report agreement, stronger dose association or more significant tests into a paper-win reward.
episode.baseline_policy: Retain native results and historical archive reconstruction as separate descriptive/calibration evidence; no authored reference or improved significance is a paper baseline.

blocking_issues: The source task has no ordered predictive or estimation-accuracy endpoint for declaring superiority.
Primary metadata does not establish the 95-session/10-animal archive mapping to published experimental panels or resolve legacy condition/detector field names.
A predictive reformulation would change the task and needs separate source-grounded registration.

legacy.notes: Preserve all original task, implementation, archive evidence and graders. The registered runtime describes archived-report fidelity and does not establish raw physiological accuracy, causal inference or stronger-than-paper performance.
